'''Jawad Hason Williams''' (born February 19, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who currently serves as an assistant coach for the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He plays as a [[small forward]]-[[power forward]]. He played high school basketball at [[St. Edward High School (Lakewood, Ohio)|St. Edward High School]] of [[Lakewood, Ohio]] (suburban [[Cleveland]]) and [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|University of North Carolina Tar Heels]].

== Early life ==
While at St. Edward, Williams played limited time as a freshman on a team anchored by [[Sam Clancy, Jr.]] and [[Steve Logan (basketball)|Steve Logan]] that went on to win the [[OHSAA]] state title.<ref>[http://www.ohiobkcoaches.com/Records/boys_state_champions.htm List of Ohio Boys State Basketball Champions] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081119232045/http://www.ohiobkcoaches.com/Records/boys_state_champions.htm |date=2008-11-19 }}</ref> During his later years in high school, he was named first team All-Ohio and named to numerous All-American teams.  He was named [[Associated Press|AP]] and [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for Ohio and played in the [[McDonald's All-American Game]].

== Collegiate career ==
Williams played [[College basketball|collegiate basketball]] under coaches [[Matt Doherty (basketball)|Matt Doherty]] and [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]]. He started as a senior for the Tar Heel team that won the [[2005 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2005 NCAA tournament]]. Williams averaged 13.1 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.4 assists in his senior season.<ref>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jawad-williams-1.html Jawad Williams Per Game.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222194226/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jawad-williams-1.html |date=2014-12-22 }}</ref> He graduated from UNC in 2005 with a B.A. in [[African-American studies]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://archive.indystar.com/data/sports/finalfour_gradrates.shtml?from=global&appSession=122139390721575 |title=Final Four Grade Rates. |access-date=2015-01-19 |archive-date=2015-01-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119072307/http://archive.indystar.com/data/sports/finalfour_gradrates.shtml?from=global&appSession=122139390721575 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Professional career ==
[[File:Jawad Williams shooting over Mike Bibby cropped.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Williams during his tenure with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]]]
Williams was not selected in the [[2005 NBA draft]]. However, he was signed as a free agent by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] of the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] during the 2006–07 season. He appeared in four preseason games for the Clippers, starting one, but did not make the final roster.

After playing in Spain, Japan and Israel,<ref name="Cavs">{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/plaindealer/index.ssf?/base/sports/122483713388720.xml&coll=2|title=St. Edward grad Jawad Williams earns spot with Cleveland Cavaliers|access-date=October 24, 2008|publisher=The Plain Dealer Newspaper|year=2008|author=Brian Windhorst|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081026040405/http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/plaindealer/index.ssf?%2Fbase%2Fsports%2F122483713388720.xml&coll=2|archive-date=October 26, 2008}}</ref><ref>[http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2010/02/jawad_williams_long_journey_br.html Jawad Williams' long journey brings him to the Cleveland Cavaliers, and home]</ref> Williams joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]' summer league team in July, 2008 and made the team's training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web | last = NBA.com  | title = Cavaliers Training Camp Roster| website = [[NBA.com]]| url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/trainingcamp_roster_080928.html}}</ref>  On October 23, the Cavs waived veteran guard [[Ronald Dupree]], and Williams became a full-fledged member of an NBA team for the first time in his career.  His contract was nonguaranteed until January 10, 2009, after which time the contract would have been guaranteed.<ref name="Cavs" />

Williams played in his first regular season NBA game and scored his first points on December 12, 2008, against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20081212/PHICLE/boxscore.html |title=76ers at Cavaliers Boxscore |work=NBA.com |access-date=2012-07-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120919213815/http://www.nba.com/games/20081212/PHICLE/boxscore.html |archive-date=2012-09-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Williams became the sixth member of North Carolina's 2005 National Championship team to play in the NBA, joining [[Rashad McCants]], [[Sean May]], [[Raymond Felton]], [[Marvin Williams]], and [[David Noel]].

Williams was waived by the Cavs on January 7, 2009. Five days after being released from the Cavs he re-signed with the team with a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/williams_waived_090107.html |title=williams_waived_090107.html Archive | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE CLEVELAND CAVALIERS |work=Nba.com |access-date=2012-07-12}}</ref> He was released on February 2 after his second 10-day contract expired. He then joined the [[NBA Development League|D-League]] with [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] on February 14. On April 8, he was re-signed to a contract for the rest of the season.
[[File:Jawad Williams Paris-Levallois action.JPG|thumb|right|upright|Williams with [[Paris-Levallois Basket|Paris-Levallois]] in 2012.]]
On February 9, 2010, Williams put up a career high in points with 17 to go along with 3  rebounds, 2 assists, and 1 steal in 28 minutes of play.

In the 2010 offseason, Jawad signed to play with the Cavs for the [[2010–11 NBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/williams_100922.html |title=Cavaliers Sign Jawad Williams | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE CLEVELAND CAVALIERS |work=Nba.com |date=2010-09-22 |access-date=2012-07-12}}</ref> On December 27, 2010, Williams was again waived by the Cavs.<ref>[http://www.crainscleveland.com/article/20101227/FREE/101229912 Cleveland Cavaliers waive Jawad Williams, assign Samardo Samuels to Erie.]</ref>

In February 2011, he signed with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] in Israel.<ref>[http://www.sport5.co.il/articles.aspx?FolderID=274&docID=94592&lang=HE ג'אוואד וויליאמס חתם בהפועל ירושלים] {{in lang|he}}</ref> For the 2011–12 season, Williams signed with [[Paris-Levallois Basket]] in France, rejoining college teammate [[David Noel]].  Williams stayed with Paris-Levallois for the 2012–13 season, but while Noel left Williams was joined by former college teammate [[Sean May]].<ref>[http://www.newsobserver.com/2013/03/10/2694650/former-tar-heels-may-williams.html Former Tar-Heels May Williams.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225151547/http://www.newsobserver.com/2013/03/10/2694650/former-tar-heels-may-williams.html |date=2014-12-25 }}</ref> Paris-Levallois waived him on January 15, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Paris-Levallois waive Jawad Williams|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/france/71712/paris-levallois-waive-jawad-williams.html|access-date=15 January 2014|newspaper=Sportando.net}}</ref> In February 2014, he signed with [[Pınar Karşıyaka]] of Turkey for the rest of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Pinar Karsiyaka signs Jawad Williams|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cat/nba/111150/pinar-karsiyaka-signs-jawad-williams.html|access-date=April 8, 2014|newspaper=Sportando.com|date=February 3, 2014}}</ref>

On June 13, 2016, Williams signed with [[AEK B.C.|AEK Athens]] in Greece for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=AEK Athens B.C. signs Williams|url=http://www.aekbc.gr/en/articles-927/aek-athens-b-c-signs-williams.htm|access-date=June 13, 2016|newspaper=Aekbc.gr|date=June 13, 2016|archive-date=November 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211123135744/http://www.aekbc.gr/en/articles-927/aek-athens-b-c-signs-williams.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 12, 2017, he parted ways with AEK.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/225910/aek-athens-jawad-williams-officially-part-ways.html AEK Athens, Jawad Williams officially part ways]</ref> The next day, he signed with Italian club [[Pallacanestro Reggiana]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/226015/pallacanestro-reggiana-announces-jawad-williams.html Pallacanestro Reggiana announces Jawad Williams]</ref>

In July 2017, Williams signed with [[Alvark Tokyo]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/asia/other-leagues/241722/jawad-williams-inks-with-toyota-alvark-tokyo.html Jawad Williams inks with Toyota Alvark Tokyo]</ref>

On June 1, 2022, he has announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketnews.com/news-172848-former-aek-player-jawad-williams-retires-from-basketball.html|title=Former AEK player Jawad Williams retires from basketball|last=|first=|date=June 1, 2022|website=basketnews.com|publisher=|language=En|access-date=June 2, 2022}}</ref>

Williams is now coaching in Japan for Nagasaki Velca. He serves as their first Assistant Coach and Director of Player Development.

==Coaching career==
In July 2022, Williams joined Nagasaki Velca of the Japanese B. League, as an assistant coach and director of player development.

On September 9, 2024, Williams was hired as an assistant coach and director of player development for the [[Sacramento Kings]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Announce Coaching Staff Updates|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-coaching-staff-updates|website=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2024|access-date=September 10, 2024}}</ref> On May 3, 2025, it was announced that Williams would be parting ways with the Kings.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Breaking: Kings Expected to Make Major Changes to Coaching Staff|url=https://www.si.com/nba/kings/sacramento-kings-news/breaking-kings-expected-to-make-major-changes-to-coaching-staff-01jtbtw19jas|access-date=June 18, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

On June 18, 2025 Williams joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] as an assistant coach under head coach [[Kenny Atkinson]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavs make hometown addition to coaching staff|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/2025/06/cavs-make-hometown-addition-to-coaching-staff.html|website=www.cleveland.com|date=June 18, 2025|access-date=June 18, 2025}}</ref>
